title: Model catalog: add stable quantization profile identifiers + metadata for cost model/Optimize
author: Benji Okafor
description: Context: The Standard Cost Model work requires a stable identifier for quantization execution profiles so telemetry, cost computation, and Optimize “what-if” scenarios can refer to the same thing over time. Today the catalog exposes quantization mostly as a free-form string (e.g. "int8", "awq", "fp16") and runtime often reports backend-specific paths; this makes joins brittle and breaks historical comparisons when naming changes. This PR adds a first-class QuantizationProfile with a stable ID and metadata, wires it into model variants, and updates catalog APIs + client types. What changed: (1) Introduced QuantizationProfile entity in the model catalog schema with a stable, opaque identifier (qprof_<base32>) and a required "spec" payload describing method + parameters; (2) ModelVariant now references quantization_profile_id (optional) while preserving the legacy quantization string for backwards compatibility; (3) Added metadata fields used by Cost Model + Optimize: bits/format, group size, activation dtype, kernel family (for runtime mapping), and constraints/notes for quality guardrails; (4) Added a deterministic ID generation rule for Redwood-managed profiles (derived from canonicalized spec + model family) and explicit override support for vendor/imported profiles; (5) Updated catalog read endpoints and SDK types; added migration/backfill job to populate IDs for existing variants; (6) Added validation + conformance tests to prevent spec drift and accidental ID churn. API details: GET /internal/model-catalog/v1/models now returns quantization_profiles[] at the model level and quantization_profile_id on variants; clients can keep reading variant.quantization for now, but new code should join on quantization_profile_id. Rollout: the server will dual-write (legacy string + id) for two releases; after Console/Optimize adoption, we can deprecate reliance on the legacy string. Risk: ID stability—addressed via canonicalization + golden fixtures; runtime mapping—kernel_family + execution_path_hint is best-effort and explicitly documented as non-contractual. Testing: unit tests for canonicalization, API serialization tests, migration job dry-run on staging snapshot, and contract tests consumed by cost-model service. Notes: Follow-ups tracked in ENG-4829 include updating the cost-model schema package to reference quantization_profile_id everywhere and a cleanup to remove old string-based joins once adoption hits >95%.
commits: model-catalog/api: return quantization_profiles and quantization_profile_id on variants
model-catalog: backfill quantization_profile_id for existing variants (offline job + dry-run)
sdk/types: regenerate catalog client types and update call sites
tests: golden fixtures for canonicalization and ID stability
review_conversation: Grace Kim: Can we guarantee that changing display name/notes doesn’t change the ID? We’ve been burned by “stable IDs” that weren’t. The runtime needs to be able to map a reported execution path back to a profile consistently across time windows.

Benji Okafor (author): Good call. ID generation is now based only on canonicalized spec + model_family + method parameters. display_name/notes/constraints are explicitly excluded. Added tests that mutate non-ID fields and assert ID is stable.

Arjun Desai: Optimize needs group_size + activation dtype to estimate throughput deltas, and we need a place to encode “quality guardrails” (e.g., disallow for certain tasks). Where is that represented and is it versioned?

Benji Okafor (author): Added spec fields: weight_format.bits, weight_format.layout, group_size, activation_dtype. Also added constraints: {recommended_for, not_recommended_for, min_quality_tier, notes}. These are metadata only; cost-model/Optimize should treat them as hints (documented). Versioning is handled by the stable ID + explicit spec; changing the spec produces a new profile ID by design.

Jonas Weber: Concern about determinism across services: if cost-model service recomputes IDs from spec it might diverge if canonicalization differs. Please make ID opaque and don’t require recomputation outside model-catalog.

Benji Okafor (author): Agree. Updated docs: ID is opaque; only model-catalog mints it. Cost-model/Optimize must treat it as a foreign key. Also removed the helper from the shared package to avoid reuse outside model-catalog.

Ethan Park: For Cost Model API latency, we’ll likely cache catalog lookups. Please keep response size bounded—adding quantization_profiles[] per model could blow up if we include too much metadata. Can we enforce a max size / field set?

Benji Okafor (author): Trimmed payload: quantization_profiles includes only id, display_name, method, core spec fields, and constraints summary. No long-form docs blobs. Added a response-size unit test and a note in docs that additional metadata must go behind a separate endpoint if needed.
Nadia Rahman: Telemetry currently reports quantization as a string; can we add an alias field so we can map older events to the new IDs during backfill windows?

Benji Okafor (author): Added aliases[] on QuantizationProfile (e.g., ["int8", "awq-int4"]) for mapping. Backfill job uses aliases + existing variant fields to attach quantization_profile_id. Telemetry join logic can use aliases until runtime exports quant_profile_id directly.
Grace Kim: One more: kernel_family looks like a contract but it’s actually best-effort. Please clarify to prevent people from depending on it for correctness.

Benji Okafor (author): Updated field comment + docs: kernel_family/execution_path_hint are non-contractual, for debugging/mapping only. Added a test that allows unknown/empty kernel_family for private deployments.
Arjun Desai: LGTM after the doc updates. Please add an example profile for “AWQ int4 g128” so Optimize can test against it.
Benji Okafor (author): Added example profiles in docs and a fixture in tests (awq_int4_g128).
Jonas Weber: Approved. Thanks for keeping the ID opaque and pushing all minting into catalog.
Ethan Park: Approved. Looks good for cost-model integration; we’ll use quantization_profile_id as the join key in v1.
Grace Kim: Approved with note: follow up to plumb quant_profile_id into runtime exports when ready (ENG-4829 dependency list).
release_notes: Internal: Model Catalog now exposes stable quantization_profile_id + quantization_profiles metadata for Cost Model and Optimize joins; legacy quantization string remains for compatibility during migration.
